mechanism: Topical ophthalmic axitinib, a VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor. SCAI describes SCAI-005 as an axitinib eye drop using MOASIS technology to deliver VEGFR TKI to posterior ocular tissues for wet AMD.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT07607561 as a not-yet-recruiting Phase 2a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel, multicenter study in neovascular wet AMD. The trial will randomize 50 subjects 2:2:1 to SCAI-005 0.04%, SCAI-005 0.08%, or placebo, with estimated start on 2026-11-01 and estimated primary/study completion on 2027-08-31. SCAI and Korean industry coverage report Phase 1 completion and Korean MFDS Phase 2 IND approval in May 2026.
expected_launch_window: 2031-2033+ if Phase 2a is positive and a partner-backed pivotal program succeeds; no defined U.S. launch path.
clinical_summary: SCAI-005 is differentiated by a non-invasive topical route in a wet AMD market dominated by intravitreal anti-VEGF injections. NCT07607561 is designed to measure change in central subfield thickness by SD-OCT at 12 weeks after SCAI-005 or placebo. The company reports preclinical posterior-tissue penetration, CNV lesion and retinal-thickness reduction in animal models, and Phase 1 tolerability in healthy volunteers. However, there are no posted patient efficacy results, the Phase 2a sample is small, and SCAI frames the product as potentially extending or reducing injection burden when used with standard injectable therapy rather than as a proven replacement.
safety_summary: The prior Phase 1 study in healthy Korean volunteers enrolled 48 subjects and assessed single/multiple ascending-dose PK, safety, and tolerability; ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results. SCAI reported excellent safety/tolerability, no ocular irritation or systemic adverse effects on its pipeline page, and no SCAI-005-related serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities in company-linked coverage. Key residual risks are unproven retinal patient safety with chronic TID dosing, local ocular tolerability, systemic VEGFR TKI exposure, and class concerns from oral axitinib such as hypertension, thromboembolism, hemorrhage, impaired wound healing, proteinuria, and hepatotoxicity, even though SCAI reports low systemic exposure for the topical formulation.
management_tools: Track Phase 2a recruitment, completion, and posted efficacy/safety results before building formulary policy.
If approved, use ophthalmology/retina-specialist diagnosis confirmation for active neovascular wet AMD.
Require baseline and follow-up OCT/central subfield thickness and visual acuity documentation for continuation.
Define whether use is adjunctive to anti-VEGF injections or substitutional; do not assume injection replacement without label-supported evidence.
Apply quantity limits aligned to final labeled regimen, likely 2 drops TID per treated eye if the studied regimen is retained.
Monitor concomitant anti-VEGF use and anti-VEGF injection interval as utilization and outcomes metrics.
Route benefit placement based on final product channel; topical self-administered drops may move part of wet AMD management from medical benefit to pharmacy benefit.
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT07607561 or the completed Phase 1 NCT06969001.
No human wet AMD efficacy data for SCAI-005 were found; available efficacy statements are preclinical and company-reported.
The public Phase 2a record measures central subfield thickness at 12 weeks but does not list BCVA as an outcome in the posted record.
SCAI-specific launch geography, regulatory strategy, pivotal-trial plan, and partner status are not publicly defined.
No SCAI-005 price exists; annual cost uses branded wet AMD anti-VEGF WAC analogs and may overstate or understate a topical axitinib product.
The 0.04% arm delivers axitinib 0.084 mg/day per ClinicalTrials.gov, but final commercial strength, bottle size, days supply, and unilateral/bilateral pricing are unknown.

sources.title: Phase 2a Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of SCAI-005 Ophthalmic Solution in Subjects With Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
supports: Sponsor is SCAI Therapeutics and study identifier is SCAI-005-201.
Overall status is not yet recruiting; Phase is Phase 2; estimated enrollment is 50.
Study design is randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel assignment, treatment purpose.
Subjects are randomized 2:2:1 to SCAI-005 0.04%, SCAI-005 0.08%, or placebo.
Intervention for the assigned asset is SCAI-005 0.04% 2drops TID with axitinib 0.084 mg/day.
Estimated study start is 2026-11-01; estimated primary completion and completion are 2027-08-31.
Primary outcome is change in central subfield thickness measured by SD-OCT at 12 weeks.
Eligibility includes adults 50 years or older with nAMD diagnosed within 3 years and prior response to at least 3 repeated intravitreal anti-VEGF injections.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.
The study is not marked as an FDA-regulated drug or device product.

sources.title: Clinical Study for the Evaluation of Safety and Tolerability of SCAI-005 Eye Drops
supports: Prior SCAI-005-101 study sponsor was SCAI Therapeutics.
Overall status is completed; actual enrollment was 48 healthy Korean volunteers.
Study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending-dose trial.
Brief summary states the trial assessed single-dose and multiple-dose PK, safety, and tolerability of SCAI-005 eyedrops (axitinib).
Multiple ascending-dose arm administered study drug three times daily for 7 days.
Primary outcome was incidence, type, and severity of adverse events over 15 days.
PK outcomes included Cmax, Tmax, t1/2, AUC, and steady-state parameters.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: SCAI-005 (Axitinib): SCAI-005: A Breakthrough Topical Therapy for Wet AMD
supports: SCAI describes SCAI-005 as an axitinib eye drop for wet AMD developed using proprietary MOASIS technology.
SCAI states the topical product is intended to enable non-invasive delivery of VEGFR TKI directly to the retina.
Company page states rabbit PK showed high posterior ocular tissue penetration with minimal systemic exposure.
Company page states monkey CNV model studies significantly reduced CNV lesion number, CNV lesion area, and retinal thickness with no observed ocular or systemic side effects.
Company page states Phase 1 clinical development was completed in November 2025.
Company page states SCAI-005 was safe and well tolerated with no ocular irritation or systemic adverse effects.
Company page states SCAI was preparing to initiate a Phase 2 clinical trial in wet AMD patients in 2026.

sources.title: SCAI Therapeutics Successfully Completes Phase 1 Clinical Trial for Wet AMD Eye Drop Candidate 'SCAI-005'
supports: SCAI announced on January 27, 2026 that SCAI-005 demonstrated excellent safety and tolerability in a domestic Phase 1 clinical trial.
SCAI described SCAI-005 as a drug candidate for neovascular age-related macular degeneration, also known as wet AMD.
Company press page said the results validate the potential of an eye drop formulation for wet AMD and support entry into Phase 2 trials.

sources.title: SCAI Therapeutics Initiates Development of an 'Inlyta-Based' Ophthalmic Drop for the Treatment of Macular Degeneration
supports: SCAI described clinical development in Korea to repurpose Inlyta (axitinib) into an ophthalmic eye drop for wet AMD.
SCAI stated it received MFDS IND approval for SCAI-005 for a Phase 1 study evaluating safety, tolerability, and PK in healthy adults.
SCAI described SCAI-005 as a reformulated ophthalmic candidate based on Inlyta, a TKI targeting VEGF receptors.
SCAI stated VEGF has a key role in pathologic angiogenesis in wet AMD.
SCAI positioned topical delivery as a strategy to deliver drug locally while minimizing systemic side effects.
SCAI cited ARVO 2021 preclinical data comparing TKI eye drops, including axitinib, with Eylea in mouse models.

sources.title: SCAI Therapeutics receives Korean Phase 2 IND approval for VEGFR eye drops in macular degeneration
supports: BioSpectator reported SCAI Therapeutics received MFDS approval on 2026-05-11 for a Phase 2 clinical trial of SCAI-005 in nAMD.
The article described SCAI-005 as an ophthalmic VEGFR TKI using axitinib as active ingredient.
The article stated SCAI expects topical administration to improve convenience and, in combination with existing therapies, reduce injection frequency or extend dosing intervals.
The article stated SCAI plans to evaluate efficacy and safety in wet AMD patients in Phase 2.
The article stated Phase 1 in healthy adults confirmed tolerability and dosing compliance, with no clinically meaningful ophthalmic safety findings and low systemic exposure.

sources.title: DailyMed: INLYTA (axitinib) tablet, film coated
supports: DailyMed lists axitinib as a kinase inhibitor approved for advanced renal cell carcinoma settings, not wet AMD.
Axitinib inhibits receptor tyrosine kinases including VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3 at therapeutic plasma concentrations.

Label warnings include hypertension, arterial and venous thromboembolic events, hemorrhage, cardiac failure, gastrointestinal perforation/fistula, impaired wound healing, RPLS, proteinuria, hepatotoxicity, and embryo-fetal toxicity.

Common adverse reactions for single-agent oral INLYTA include diarrhea, hypertension, fatigue, decreased appetite, nausea, dysphonia, hand-foot syndrome, weight decreased, vomiting, asthenia, and constipation.

sources.title: DailyMed: EYLEA HD (aflibercept) injection, solution
supports: EYLEA HD is indicated for neovascular wet AMD and is a VEGF inhibitor.
Recommended nAMD dosing is 8 mg by intravitreal injection every 4 weeks for the first three doses, followed by once every 8 to 16 weeks.
Some patients may need to resume every-4-week dosing if they do not maintain response after successful response to the first three monthly doses.
Warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis with or without occlusion, increases in intraocular pressure, and potential arterial thromboembolic events.

Common adverse reactions include cataract, conjunctival hemorrhage, corneal epithelium defect, intraocular pressure increased, ocular discomfort/eye pain/eye irritation, retinal hemorrhage, blurred vision, vitreous detachment, and vitreous floaters.

sources.title: EYLEA HD Colorado Drug Cost Education
supports: EYLEA HD 8 mg single-dose vial and vial kit WAC price was $2,812.98 as of 2026-01-09.
WAC is the manufacturer's undiscounted list price and does not include prompt pay discounts, rebates, or other reductions.
Patient cost varies by insurance and benefit design.

sources.title: DailyMed: VABYSMO (faricimab-svoa) injection, solution
supports: VABYSMO is indicated for neovascular wet AMD and inhibits VEGF and Ang-2.
Recommended nAMD dosing is 6 mg by intravitreal injection every 4 weeks for the first 4 doses, followed by OCT and visual-acuity guided regimens at Weeks 20, 24, 28, 36, 44, or 48.
Some patients may need monthly dosing after the first 4 doses.
Warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachments, increases in intraocular pressure, and potential arterial thromboembolic events associated with VEGF inhibition.

sources.title: Information for Colorado Prescribers of Prescription Drugs: VABYSMO
supports: Vabysmo 6 mg/0.05 mL syringe and vial WAC package price was $2,346.89.
WAC does not represent actual transaction prices and excludes discounts, rebates, and price reductions.
Document states no generic drugs in the same therapeutic class were listed.

sources.title: Cigna Drug and Biologic Coverage Policy: Faricimab (Vabysmo)
supports: Cigna applies medical necessity criteria to Vabysmo coverage.
For neovascular wet AMD, initial approval duration is up to 12 months.
Continuation requires documentation of beneficial response and meeting medical necessity criteria.
Any other use is considered experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Policy uses HCPCS J2777 for injection, faricimab-svoa, 0.1 mg.

expected_launch_window.value: 2031-2033+ if Phase 2a is positive and a partner-backed pivotal program succeeds; no defined U.S. launch path.
expected_launch_window.method: Started from estimated Phase 2a completion in August 2027, then assumed additional dose selection, pivotal development, regulatory review, and commercialization work because no pivotal or filing plan is public.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The asset is early Phase 2a, not yet recruiting, and SCAI has publicly discussed Phase 2 evaluation and external collaboration rather than a direct launch timeline.

annual_cost_range.method: Used EYLEA HD branded wet AMD WAC as the closest current high-cost anti-VEGF treatment analog: $2,812.98 per dose x 5 to 8 first-year injections = $14,064.90 to $22,503.84, rounded to whole dollars.
annual_cost_range.explanation: No SCAI-005 price, bottle size, days supply, or net cost exists. Because SCAI-005 is intended to affect wet AMD injection burden, branded anti-VEGF WAC provides a conservative wet AMD analog, not a forecast of final topical axitinib pricing.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced a potentially meaningful non-invasive topical route and preclinical posterior-segment activity against absence of human wet AMD efficacy data, small Phase 2a size, and continued likely use with anti-VEGF injections.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: If Phase 2a shows CST and vision benefit with reduced injection burden, differentiation could become meaningful; current evidence remains too early for that rating.

budget_impact.method: Rated from early-stage uncertainty, potential chronic TID topical use in a high-prevalence retinal population, possible adjunctive use on top of injections, and high current branded anti-VEGF analog costs.
budget_impact.explanation: Budget impact is not immediate, but a topical adjunct could add pharmacy spend while affecting medical-benefit injection utilization if efficacy is confirmed.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from route-of-administration disruption potential, possible benefit-channel shift from physician-administered injection to self-administered topical therapy, and long development runway.
disruption_risk.explanation: Operational disruption would be meaningful if topical SCAI-005 reduces injection frequency, but Phase 2a has not started and no patient efficacy data are available.

recommended_action.method: Recommended monitoring because NCT07607561 is not yet recruiting, has a small Phase 2a design, and lacks posted human wet AMD efficacy results.
recommended_action.explanation: No active formulary build is warranted yet; reassess when Phase 2a recruitment, CST/BCVA results, safety, dosing, partnering, and regulatory plans become public.

quality_flags: Very early wet AMD patient evidence: NCT07607561 is not yet recruiting and no patient efficacy results are posted.
Phase 1 completed in healthy volunteers, not wet AMD patients; ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted Phase 1 results.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists the trial as not FDA-regulated, so near-term U.S. regulatory implications are unclear.
Company-reported preclinical and Phase 1 safety claims are supportive but not a substitute for posted clinical results or peer-reviewed wet AMD patient data.
Cost estimate is analog-based from branded intravitreal anti-VEGF WAC and should be replaced when SCAI-005 pricing, package size, benefit channel, and final dosing are known.
The public Phase 2a record focuses on 12-week central subfield thickness; visual acuity benefit and injection-burden reduction are important unproven commercial differentiators.
